title: 大気の川と水管理
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: Editorial answers（編集・確認した解答）。元の本文・解説に基づき記述設問を英語4択へ変換しています。元記事の記述問題も引き続き利用できます。

passages.text:
An atmospheric river is a long, narrow, transient corridor of strong horizontal water-vapor transport. It is not a river of liquid water, nor is every moist cloud band an atmospheric river. Scientists identify the phenomenon by combining humidity and wind through the depth of the lower atmosphere. When the flow reaches a coast or mountain range, rising air can cool and condense, producing substantial rain or snow.

The result is not inherently beneficial or destructive. A moderate event can replenish reservoirs, build mountain snowpack, and interrupt drought. A strong or long-lasting event can produce flooding, landslides, or debris flows. Impact depends not only on vapor transport but also on storm duration and orientation, terrain, freezing level, soil moisture, reservoir conditions, and exposure of people and infrastructure. The same measured transport can therefore lead to different outcomes at different locations or times.

Forecasting converts this physical distinction into a management problem. Satellite observations show the broad moisture corridor, while aircraft, ocean buoys, radar, and ground instruments measure its structure and landfall. Forecasts of intensity, duration, freezing level, and runoff can support flood warnings and reservoir decisions. Releasing water before a storm may create storage space, but an unnecessary release can waste supply. Managers need probabilistic forecasts, explicit risk thresholds, and updated observations rather than a single label.

A warmer atmosphere can contain more water vapor when other conditions are comparable, so future atmospheric rivers may carry more moisture and produce heavier precipitation. That thermodynamic expectation is stronger than a claim that every region will experience more events. Changes in storm tracks, winds, frequency, and landfall location also depend on atmospheric dynamics and vary among projections. Adaptation must therefore prepare for greater moisture potential while preserving uncertainty about where and how often the most damaging combinations will occur.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Every atmospheric river should be treated as a disaster.

options.label: B
options.text: Atmospheric rivers are liquid rivers located above mountains.

options.label: C
options.text: Their impacts emerge from vapor transport interacting with duration, terrain, prior conditions, and human decisions.

options.label: D
options.text: Climate warming determines exactly where every future event will make landfall.

questions.answer: Impacts depend on interacting conditions, not the event's name alone. 正解：C。水蒸気輸送・地形・先行条件・判断の関係が主旨です。Aは水資源への利益を無視し、Bは水蒸気を液体と混同。Dは上陸場所の不確実性を消しています。

questions.prompt: Why is a moist cloud band's appearance insufficient to identify an atmospheric river?

options.label: A
options.text: Identification depends on humidity and wind through the depth of the lower atmosphere, not appearance alone.

options.label: B
options.text: Cloud bands contain liquid rivers that cannot be observed from satellites.

options.label: C
options.text: Only precipitation after landfall determines whether horizontal transport exists.

options.label: D
options.text: Scientists identify atmospheric rivers by altitude alone, regardless of wind.

questions.answer: The definition concerns horizontal water-vapor transport. 正解：A。humidity（湿度）とwind（風）を大気の厚みにわたり組み合わせる必要があります。Bの液体の川、Cの上陸後だけという限定、Dの標高だけという定義は本文にありません。

questions.prompt: Which group lists three factors that can change impacts even when measured vapor transport is similar?

options.label: A
options.text: The event's name, the day of the week, and the observer's nationality

options.label: B
options.text: Cloud color alone, calendar month alone, and the name of the nearest city

options.label: C
options.text: Only vapor transport, because soil and terrain cannot affect consequences

options.label: D
options.text: Storm duration, terrain, and prior soil moisture

questions.answer: Paragraph 2 lists duration, terrain, and soil moisture among the relevant conditions. 正解：D。prior soil moistureは「事象前からの土壌水分」。輸送量が同じでもこれらが結果を変えます。A・Bは本文にない分類、Cはnot only ... but alsoという説明を否定します。

questions.prompt: The phrase 'not inherently beneficial or destructive' in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to:

options.label: A
options.text: its effect is determined without regard to context

options.label: B
options.text: it has no possible effect on water supply

options.label: C
options.text: its consequences depend on interacting conditions

options.label: D
options.text: only weak events can be measured

questions.answer: Inherently means by its nature, without depending on circumstances. 正解：C。inherently（本質的に・性質上）を否定し、条件の組合せで利益にも被害にもなると述べます。Aは逆、Bは水供給への効果を否定し、Dは観測できる強度を不当に限定します。

questions.prompt: How do satellite observations and the other instruments complement one another in paragraph 3?

options.label: A
options.text: Satellites measure reservoir releases, while other instruments identify events solely by cloud color.

options.label: B
options.text: Satellites show the broad moisture corridor, while aircraft, buoys, radar, and ground instruments measure its structure and landfall.

options.label: C
options.text: Satellites predict every local impact exactly, so other measurements are unnecessary.

options.label: D
options.text: Other instruments only name the event, while satellites alone make management decisions.

questions.answer: Broad coverage and measurements of structure and landfall provide complementary information. 正解：B。complementaryは「互いに補い合う」。広域の水蒸気帯と詳しい構造・上陸の観測を組み合わせます。Aは役割を改変し、Cは精度を過大視、Dは観測と管理判断を混同します。

questions.prompt: Why do pre-storm reservoir releases require probabilistic forecasts and explicit risk thresholds?

options.label: A
options.text: Every release improves both flood safety and water supply regardless of rainfall.

options.label: B
options.text: A single event label specifies the correct release volume for all reservoirs.

options.label: C
options.text: Releasing water always makes additional storage space unnecessary.

options.label: D
options.text: Releases can create flood-storage space, but unnecessary releases can waste water supply.

questions.answer: Managers must weigh flood protection against possible supply loss. 正解：D。probabilistic forecasts（確率予報）は複数の可能性を示し、risk thresholds（リスク閾値）は行動を変える基準です。A・Bは条件を無視した万能化、Cは放流で空き容量をつくる説明と逆です。

questions.prompt: Why does warming not directly establish that every region will experience more atmospheric rivers?

options.label: A
options.text: Frequency and landfall also depend on atmospheric dynamics, whose projected regional changes vary.

options.label: B
options.text: Warmer air cannot contain more moisture under comparable conditions.

options.label: C
options.text: Atmospheric rivers occur independently of winds and storm tracks.

options.label: D
options.text: All projections agree that moisture potential and frequency are the same quantity.

questions.answer: Moisture potential and regional event frequency are different claims. 正解：A。atmospheric dynamics（大気力学：風や嵐の運動に関わる過程）も頻度・経路を左右します。Bは本文の含水量の説明と逆、Cは力学を無視し、Dは別の量を同一視しています。

questions.prompt: Why does the author contrast 'may carry more moisture' with the claim that every region 'will experience more events'?

options.label: A
options.text: The author regards both claims as equally certain predictions for every location.

options.label: B
options.text: The author uses 'may' to deny any physical basis for increased moisture.

options.label: C
options.text: The author distinguishes a conditional, stronger thermodynamic expectation from a less certain universal frequency claim.

options.label: D
options.text: The author states that heavier precipitation is impossible unless event frequency rises everywhere.

questions.answer: The contrast marks different evidential strength and scope. 正解：C。thermodynamic（熱力学的な）含水量の予想と、全地域での頻度増加を区別します。Aは確実性を同じにし、Bはmayを否定と誤読。Dの必要条件は本文にありません。

questions.prompt: Which reservoir operating plan best applies the passage's reasoning?

options.label: A
options.text: Release the same volume before every named atmospheric river, without updating observations.

options.label: B
options.text: Update release decisions using flood probabilities, storage and supply targets, and new observations as the storm approaches.

options.label: C
options.text: Never release water before a storm, because maintaining supply is the only relevant objective.

options.label: D
options.text: Empty the reservoir after any warning, even when later forecasts lower the flood probability.

questions.answer: The plan must respond to new evidence while balancing storage and safety. 正解：B。本文の発展記述を、考え方の適用を問う選択問題に変換しました。Aは一律運用、Cは洪水対策を無視、Dは供給損失と更新情報を無視するため不適切です。
